messages:
alex: Hi all, quick onboarding snag on day 1 — followed the internal dotfiles bootstrap but my dev shell isn't picking up node/pnpm from the npm-global prefix and asdf won't install python. Machine is a corporate Mac (shows Intel in About). I get `pnpm: command not found` even after re-installing. Any obvious things to check?

mira: welcome! :wave: Which shell are you using (zsh/fish/bash)? The bootstrap symlinks a zshrc but people sometimes still end up on bash. Also do `echo $SHELL` and `echo $PATH`.

alex: `echo $SHELL` -> /bin/zsh. PATH prints lots of entries, but I see /usr/bin before /Users/alex/.asdf/shims. My ~/.zshrc has the dotfiles symlink and a line `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"`.

corey: if shims are after /usr/bin they'll be shadowed. Make sure asdf shims are sourced and appear earlier. Typical lines we keep near top of ~/.zshrc: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"\n. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh\n. $(brew --prefix asdf)/etc/profile.d/asdf.sh` The order matters.

alex: I do have `export PATH` at the top but not the two `asdf.sh` lines. I added them and restarted shell but `asdf list` still empty.

mira: after sourcing asdf you still need to install runtimes. Check `~/.tool-versions`. The dotfiles set nothing by default, we rely on per-repo `.tool-versions` and direnv. Do `asdf plugin-list` to see installed plugins. For node we prefer asdf nodejs plugin over nvm in the dotfiles so there's a consistent global location for pnpm.

alex: `asdf plugin-list` returns `python nodejs` (so plugins present). `asdf list` shows nothing. Trying `asdf install python 3.10.9` fails with a compile error referencing openssl headers.

corey: classic — macOS needs the brew libs. `brew install openssl readline xz zlib` then set build flags: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl)/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl)/include"` before `asdf install`. On Intel look at `brew --prefix` — intel uses /usr/local, arm uses /opt/homebrew.

alex: interesting: `which brew` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/brew even though About says Intel. How should I reconcile?

mira: someone likely installed Homebrew for arm prefix previously (brew supports multiple installs but it's messy). Use `brew --prefix` to build flags (so `$(brew --prefix openssl)` will still work). Alternatively reinstall Homebrew for the correct arch to avoid cross-compiled bottles issues. For now, using `$(brew --prefix ...)` is fine.

corey: about pnpm: npm global prefix can be set by `npm config get prefix`. If that points to a system dir (/usr/local) npm will attempt to install there and require sudo. Run `mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-global" && npm config set prefix "$HOME/.npm-global"` then add `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` to ~/.zshrc before any other PATH rewrites. After that `npm i -g pnpm` should land in your home dir.

alex: ran the openssl brew install and the exports, then `asdf install python 3.10.9` succeeded after a while. Also set npm prefix and reinstalled pnpm, now `which pnpm` -> /Users/alex/.npm-global/bin/pnpm.

mira: nice. One more gotcha: direnv is used to load per-repo .tool-versions/envrc. Make sure `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` is in your zshrc and run `direnv allow` in the repo so asdf/local versions get applied. Without that you might still see a different python from system.

alex: I didn't have the direnv hook. Added it and `direnv allow` in the project root. `asdf current` now shows python 3.10.9 and node 18.17.0 (node came from package.json .tool-versions). Everything seems green.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-512: "onboarding: document brew intel vs arm edge case + asdf direnv steps" and assigned to @mira.

alex: thanks everyone 64f I'll open a tiny PR to the dotfiles README noting the importance of the asdf.sh lines and npm prefix ordering. Appreciate the quick help!
